sourceSentence: The family gives the child a secure base.

ownerComparison.finding: Defensibly distinct: canonical 1526 home base is a broad place/source of support; new 4680 base camp is a logistical departure/return point. Secure base here teaches a child–trusted-adult relationship enabling exploration and return for reassurance, supported by public attachment/education guidance.

traditionalChinese.finding: 安全基地 is established Traditional Chinese terminology for secure base in Hong Kong public guidance; the lesson translations are generally faithful.

checks.answerKeyGrounding: All keyed scene/contrast/dialogue/listening answers defensible; reply options C/D need completion.

findings.issue: The prompt gives two concrete wishes: a parent at pickup and the daughter choosing her own project. Option C discusses a possible leader check-in and project choice but never commits to pickup; D arranges a meeting afterwards without explicitly preserving the project choice. The SOP requires each of four replies to answer independently.
findings.repair: Make C and D explicitly cover pickup and child choice, while retaining distinct valid suggestions. Keep A as the sole target-bearing golden reply and align EN/ZH.

findings.issue: The speaking model labels a teacher a secure base based only on being a help point during one first school trip. In attachment/education usage the term implies a dependable relationship that supports exploration, not merely a one-time directions contact.
findings.repair: Add an established trust/ongoing support cue to the same spoken model, retain the child independently interviewing the guide, align Chinese and recalculate targetSpan if affected.
